The fixed rational tables replace the canonical completion-parameter and conditional-Bernoulli description; that description and the separately named A/N probabilities are not theorem conjuncts. The Challenge docstring discloses this reduction. Independent exact arithmetic reconstructed all 17 masses of each canonical Bernoulli construction and checked every asserted numerical moment, observed cell, and positive conditional-mean denominator. Thus the concrete laws really are the claimed witnesses; using the finite subclass for nonidentification is sufficient, not a hidden causal assumption. This refutes the point-identification reading of the application, not its printed numerical estimates.

States the joint-moment identities, the sufficient mixed respondent mean equalities with all required positivity, conditional response-independence implication, cell reweighting with empty cells omitted, unconditional sensitivity inequalities, and all eight exact source-table calculations. It does not state the canonical assertion that cellwise mean ignorability alone need not give arm-mean equality, or attainment of the four sensitivity endpoints and consequent sharpness for the observed source law. Both omissions are disclosed in the Challenge docstring. Its joint-event positivity hypotheses are equivalent to the canonical conditional positivity because the conditioning arms/cells are positive. Uniform independent S in {A,N,C} and Z in {0,1}, Y0=0,Y1=1, R=1, satisfies all nontrivial identification premises simultaneously.

Matches canonical (i)-(iv): arbitrary real inputs with 0<p<1; equivalence of mixture and corrected systems; the unique recovered n; elimination of x0; all interval and endpoint translations; the actual weaker printed residual constraint; and one strict non-equivalence witness. No e0/e1 boundedness is silently added. For example p=1/2,e0=e1=3/4,x0=x1=1,n=1/2 satisfies the mixture constraints. All divisions occur with p>0 or 1-p>0.

States the exact E1-E4 counterexample, failure of both corrected and mixture systems, and all four numerical interval endpoints. For E6 retains existence of an admissible bounded model with the specified input moments and c0=c1=1, without specifying half never-takers of outcome 1/2 or fair assignment. These omissions are precisely disclosed. The canonical E6 construction itself is a nonvacuity witness. This is a counterexample to the printed reframing, not to Proposition 1's intervals.

It does not itself exhibit that p=1 is possible; nor does it state the optional positive-pure-cell probability-times-mean representation or separately assert zero product moment for an empty cell. The docstring discloses exactly these omissions. The noncomplier event mean is used as an ordinary mean only under p<1. Fair full compliance and the six-point mixed-stratum model give feasible instances, including both boundary branches.

The fixed fair two-atom law has exactly the canonical potentials and observed variables, proves random assignment for every predicate of the latent atom, and states F1-F6 including the failed side conditions: null noncomplier and pure-cell events, zero numerators and denominators, arbitrary-n mixture identities, and singleton bounds. It never treats the value of totalized 0/0 as a refutation. This diagnoses an unqualified proof step; it does not refute the proposition or the corollary under its positive-cell premise.

States both printed intervals for every bounded randomized monotone causal model, and genuinely sharp attainment of every point of each coordinate interval for every compatible triple 0<p<=1, e0,e1 in [0,1], |e1-e0|<=p. Existential witnesses use a separate nonempty four-point sample space, rather than the arbitrary ambient type, and include p=1. No extra treatment-cell probabilities or noncomplier split is fixed. Pointwise bounded measurable potentials imply global integrability, so CausalModel's moment fields add no restriction here. For p<1 use p compliers with potentials (x1-delta,x1), 1-p never-takers with both potentials (e1-p*x1)/(1-p), and independent fair assignment; for p=1 use only compliers with potentials (e0,e1). Exact grid checks support the algebra but are not used as a universal proof.

Retains the positive-cell ordinary-mean premise, recovery of arm means, stratum probabilities and means, the noncomplier ratio, and both complier formulas. CausalModel additionally requires measurable and globally absolutely integrable Y0 and Y1. The canonical finite observed cell means constrain only observed and complier moments, not the counterfactual Y0 on A or Y1 on N, so this is a real domain restriction, notwithstanding the weaker audit-history note about sufficient integrable potentials. The Challenge docstring explicitly and accurately discloses it. Uniform S and fair independent Z with Y0=0,Y1=1 satisfies all four positive cells; all denominator masses are then positive.

The universal first-stage, reduced-form and both LATE ratios require both potential outcomes to be measurable and globally absolutely integrable through CausalModel. Finite observed-arm and complier-effect means do not constrain unused potentials on noncompliers, so this is a genuine extra hypothesis relative to the canonical display; it is explicitly disclosed in the docstring. The nonidentification conjunct retains the full intended existential claim, with bounded witnesses p=1/2,e0=e1=3/4,tau=0 and levels (1/2,1/2) versus (1,1). It correctly fixes just the three reported scalar figures, not the entire observed law, and does not claim nonidentification for every triple.
